cases.reason: The reported source selects the local installation, profile, workspace, output or cache root under the launching user's authority. The CLI and native host intentionally access that selected root without elevation. Reading the root from argv/environment or an OS folder API is not an unauthorized path selection by a different principal. This decision covers the exact exported source-to-sink trace, not unrelated archive leaf paths, hostile concurrent writers, elevated launches or plugin sandboxing.
Retained for the associated code repair and follow-up scan/acceptance; not counted as a false positive or a GitHub closure. See the individual source/sink and fix mapping in the review ledger.

The reported taint selects a caller-authorized local executable (the packaged Node/native host, Windows system tool, browser, or test compiler). The inspected invocation supplies separate arguments or the native Windows quoting routine. It is not an inbound request concatenated into an arbitrary shell command. This assumes the launching user's installation and launch environment are trusted; a malicious plugin already executing in-process is not sandboxed.

The exported source is process.argv[1] or ComSpec from the launching user. dshArgv resolves an existing bin.js/bin.ts/dsh entry and selects viaShell=false, so Portable re-invokes its Node executable with an argument array. The separate fallback for an explicitly selected PATH .cmd shim uses the same user's shell. This decision concerns the exported executable-selection flow, not a general proof that arbitrary cmd.exe argument interpolation is safe.

Three.js generateUUID labels scene/resource objects for the static product website. The identifier is not an authentication token, password, session credential, capability or cryptographic secret. Unpredictability is not a security requirement for this use.

The evaluated text is checked-out repository JavaScript or an explicit maintainer test-source override, used to exercise that code with test doubles. The same repository author/caller already controls executable test code. No lower-trust remote payload is promoted to executable code by the reported source. A Node VM is not being treated as a security sandbox.

checkClientBundle constructs new Script(source) only to check syntax; it never calls runInContext, runInNewContext or runInThisContext on that Script. Compiling JavaScript text does not execute that text. The separate package-file containment issue is tracked in the held path alerts.

JSON.stringify serializes fixture button names as a JavaScript literal sent to CDP Runtime.evaluate. The value is not embedded in an HTML script element, so the HTML closing-script context that motivates this rule is absent. These names are also repository-owned test fixtures.

The reported timer input passes through boundedTimeout before setTimeout: non-finite, zero and negative inputs use the fixed default; positive values are floored and capped. Installation/provider timers are capped at 3600000 ms and hot activation at 60000 ms. Regression tests exercise NaN, infinities, fractions and values above the Node timer range.

The requested URL and expected SHA-256 come from the repository-owned upstream.lock.json. The Windows compiler contract intentionally downloads that pinned SDK and verifies its bytes. There is no attacker HTTP parameter or cross-principal server proxy in the reported flow.

This maintainer smoke test reads the process state of the product it just launched and probes only URL.origin, with redirects disabled and a 2000 ms timeout. The one-time credential is deliberately not replayed. The reported source is the test's own local runtime state, not an untrusted request proxy target.

The URL uses the fixed https://api.github.com/repos/ origin; repository metadata comes from checked-out docs/official-desktop-baseline.json. A caller cannot change the destination host through an inbound request in this maintainer command.

This is the explicit local dsh CLI plugin archive download requested in process.argv, not a server fetching a URL on behalf of an untrusted remote principal. Downloading the URL chosen by the launching user is intended behavior; HTTP(S) archive recognition and size limits remain in place.

The registry endpoint originates in the launching user's DSHM_REGISTRY_URL configuration. Private registries/proxies are intentional configuration, not an HTTP caller-controlled SSRF destination. This is limited to the supplied configuration-source flow.

The commondir file is Git worktree metadata in the launching user's local checkout. Following it to locate the common Git directory is intentional; the code reads repository identity, not an executable command or a network-supplied file path. This is not permission to trust arbitrary imported archives or elevated launches.

The preview runtime job is disabled for pull_request events. The upstream checkout ref is read from the tracked lockfile, git rev-parse verifies that exact reviewed commit, and native jobs consume artifacts from the same run. The reported workflow_dispatch path runs owner-approved source; it does not combine an attacker PR checkout with a privileged main-branch cache consumer. Trust in the approved upstream source remains explicit.
